slides.text: “Sex toys are for people who can’t find a partner.”

slides.statement: of women in a national US study had used a vibrator.
slides.detail: Nearly 1 in 4 had used one in the past month.
slides.source: Source: Herbenick et al., _Journal of Sexual Medicine_, 2009. 2,056 US women aged 18–60.

slides.statement: of heterosexual men who had used a vibrator used it with a female partner, during foreplay or sex.
slides.detail: Men’s use was common too: 44.8% had used one.
slides.source: Source: Reece et al., _Journal of Sexual Medicine_, 2009. 1,047 US men aged 18–60.

slides.headline: A toy isn’t a replacement for a partner. For many couples, it’s *part of how they enjoy each other.*
slides.body: Women who used vibrators also scored higher on desire, arousal and orgasm. That’s a link, not proof that the toy caused it.
slides.note: These are US figures. We haven’t found Nigerian data on this yet.

slides.headline: Wanting more pleasure doesn’t mean *something is missing.*
slides.lead: Save this for the next time someone says it.

captions.instagram:
Myth: sex toys are for people who can’t find a partner.

In a national US study, 52.5% of women had used a vibrator. And 91% of heterosexual men who had used one used it with a female partner. A toy isn’t a replacement for love. For many couples, it’s part of it.

Save this for the next time someone says it.

Sources: Herbenick et al. and Reece et al., Journal of Sexual Medicine, 2009. US adults aged 18–60. Both studies were funded by Church & Dwight Co.

#MythVsFact #SexualWellness #PleasureIsSelfCare #Relationships #Intimova
